question: How does billing work?

key_facts.text: Billing uses meter reading results or load profiles to determine the evaluation basis for schema execution. All calculations required for rate creation are made during schema execution. Different billing periods are included in the various billing procedures. All master and billing master data can change during a billing period. The billing module ensures that all billing-relevant changes that occur during a billing period are taken into consideration. For example, a price change causes the system to divide the total period into subperiods, each with the price valid for that subperiod. The system also divides the total consumption, which produces the corresponding partial amount.

question: Tell me about Processing Budget Billing Plans.

key_facts.text: When periodic billing documents are invoiced, a new budget billing plan is created automatically for contracts that were billed periodically. The budget billing plan is based on the budget billing extrapolation lines, which are generated by the billing document. A reference to the bill to be created is stored in the header of the budget billing plan in the Inv. doc. no. field (invoicing document number), so that information about future budget billings is shown on the bill. For information about other options for grouping budget billings of the different contracts of a budget billing plan, see the documentation for the Budget Billing Plan (IS-U-IN-BB) component.

key_facts.text: This component enables you to create and manage contract account master data. In Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, each business partner posting is assigned to one business partner and to one contract account. In the contract account master record, you can define, for each business partner, the procedures that apply when posting and processing the line items of a given contract account. These include, for example, payment and dunning.

question: How does invoicing create the link to contract accounting?

key_facts.text: Invoicing creates the link to contract accounting and provides the basis for bill creation. The contracts of a contract account are grouped together in invoicing for the joint bill. Posting documents are posted in subledger accounting. Budget billing plans are processed.

notes: Related question from frontend follow-up pool: How does invoicing create the link to contract accounting?

question: How does move-in processing work?

key_facts.text: You use the move-in function to carry out most of the activities required to begin providing a business partner with a utility service. You create new, or change existing business master data. Most importantly, you allocate a contract to an installation.

notes: Related question from frontend follow-up pool: How does move-in processing work?

question: How does move-out processing work?

key_facts.text: During the move-out transaction, you execute most of the activities required to cancel the customer's supply of utilities services. You make changes to the business partner master data that result from a move-out. You specifically end the allocation of a contract to an installation on the move-out date.

notes: Related question from frontend follow-up pool: How does move-out processing work?

question: How does automatic billing work?

key_facts.text: Automatic billing enables you to bill a single contract or any selection of contracts. Contracts not allocated to an installation are not selected. Billing is executed based on intervals defined in scheduling. All master data that form the basis of the contract – such as the installation, device or register – are automatically taken into account.
